rules.title: No tool attribution in change text
rules.statement: Commit messages, pull request titles and bodies, merge bodies, issue text and release notes MUST NOT carry any trailer naming an AI tool or its no-reply address (Co-Authored-By, Signed-off-by, Reviewed-by, Assisted-by and the like), any footer saying the text was generated, written or made with a tool, or the robot emoji beside such a footer. The signer is the operator of record for the change. A trailer that names a role rather than a product, such as Operated-by: agent, is not attribution and is permitted.
rules.fix: Remove the trailer or footer; the sign-off already names who answers for the change.

deny: gh pr create --title t --body "Done. Generated with Claude Code"

printf 'Note

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
' > msg.txt && git commit -F msg.txt
ask: git commit -m "Add Claude Code plugin manifest"

rules.title: Strict mode: no vendor mention in change text
rules.statement: When a repository sets attribution.mode to strict, the same text MUST NOT mention a listed vendor or product name at all, in any case or spelling.
rules.notes: Off by default so a repository can say which tools it supports in its own history.
rules.fix: Reword without the vendor name, or switch attribution.mode back to patterns for this repository.

rules.title: Stage by path
rules.statement: An agent MUST NOT run git add -A, --all or -u without a narrowing pathspec, git add with a root pathspec such as ".", or git commit -a, unless the repository switches the check off (stage.deny_add_all, stage.deny_commit_all). Changes are staged by path and checked with git diff --cached --stat before the commit.
rules.fix: Stage the files by name (git add <path>), check git diff --cached --stat, then commit.

rules.title: No force push to a protected branch
rules.statement: A force push (--force, -f, --force-with-lease, --force-if-includes, or a + refspec) to a protected branch MUST NOT be issued from an agent session. A protected branch moves by merged pull request only.
rules.fix: Push the branch and open a pull request; a protected branch moves by merge.

rules.title: Moving a tag is confirmed and explained
rules.statement: A force push of a tag MUST be confirmed by the user, and the reason shown MUST say that every workflow triggered on tag pushes runs again at that tag.
rules.fix: If the tag must move, expect every tag-triggered workflow to run again and release assets to be rebuilt.

rules.title: No key-shaped literals
rules.statement: Staged changes MUST NOT contain key-shaped literals: cloud access keys, forge and registry tokens, private key blocks, bearer tokens, or signing secrets, in code, tests, fixtures or documentation samples. Tests generate keys at runtime. The staged scan can be switched off for a repository (secrets.scan_staged).
rules.fix: Unstage the file, move the value to the environment or a secret store, and generate test keys at runtime.

rules.title: A commit waits for a go-ahead
rules.statement: Every git commit an agent issues, including --amend, MUST be confirmed by the user before it runs, unless the repository sets confirm.commit to false.
rules.fix: Show the staged change and the message; commit when the user says yes.

rules.title: A push waits for a go-ahead
rules.statement: Every git push an agent issues MUST be confirmed by the user before it runs, unless the repository sets confirm.push to false.
rules.fix: Say what is pushed and where; push when the user says yes.

rules.title: A post waits for a go-ahead
rules.statement: Every command that creates or changes something on a forge (a pull request, review, comment, issue, release, label, repository setting or an API write) MUST be confirmed by the user before it runs, unless the repository sets confirm.post to false. A draft is shown in the conversation first.
rules.fix: Show the draft in the conversation; post when the user says yes.

rules.title: Lead with the decision
rules.statement: A message or document written for a reader MUST open with the answer, the decision or the outcome; evidence follows. A scope cut or a miss goes in the first line.

rules.title: Current state only
rules.statement: Shared documents MUST state the current state. They MUST NOT narrate earlier versions, carry version or branch labels in prose, or describe a target as "today X, later Y".

rules.title: No dashes as punctuation
rules.statement: Text SHOULD NOT use an em dash or a spaced en dash to join clauses. End the sentence or use a comma.
rules.notes: Coincides with unslop (cursor/plugins, pstack). CI enforces it through lint-voice over the paths the caller passes as voice-paths; without them the rule is skill text.

rules.title: No rhetorical structure
rules.statement: Text SHOULD NOT use counting framings ("two things", "three fixes"), triads for rhythm, "that is why", or an aphoristic closing line.
rules.notes: The triads clause coincides with unslop (cursor/plugins, pstack). The lint catches counting framings and "that is why"; triads and aphorisms are judged by the reader. CI enforces it through lint-voice over the paths the caller passes as voice-paths; without them the rule is skill text.

rules.title: End when the content ends
rules.statement: Text SHOULD NOT close with an offer to help or walk through, a chatbot phrase, or a restatement of what was just said, and MUST NOT open with praise for the question.
rules.notes: Coincides with unslop (cursor/plugins, pstack). CI enforces it through lint-voice over the paths the caller passes as voice-paths; without them the rule is skill text.

rules.title: Banned words
rules.statement: Text SHOULD NOT use seamless, robust, best-in-class, leverage, comprehensive, world-class, delve, tapestry, testament, cutting-edge or game-changing. Say the measured thing instead.
rules.notes: Coincides with unslop (cursor/plugins, pstack). CI enforces it through lint-voice over the paths the caller passes as voice-paths; without them the rule is skill text.

rules.title: No throat clearing
rules.statement: Text SHOULD NOT open a sentence with "it is worth noting", "note that", "importantly", "in summary" or similar; the sentence stands without the preface.
rules.notes: Coincides with unslop (cursor/plugins, pstack). CI enforces it through lint-voice over the paths the caller passes as voice-paths; without them the rule is skill text.

rules.title: Evidence words carry evidence
rules.statement: "Live", "100%", "PASS", "confirmed", "resolved", "on track" and "zero data loss" MUST NOT appear without the evidence that earns them: an evidence tag, a sha, a date, a lane, or a gate. "Green" is never a status; give the sha, the date and the lane.
rules.notes: The lint warns on the words when no evidence tag shares the line; the reader judges the rest. CI enforces it through lint-voice over the paths the caller passes as voice-paths; without them the rule is skill text.

rules.title: Tag every claim
rules.statement: Every factual clause in a deliverable MUST carry one of Verified (the source was opened), Measured (a number with its query), Inferred, or Planned. A level is never upgraded: merged is not deployed, and deployed is not verified in data.

rules.title: Verify at the production sha
rules.statement: A claim about running behaviour MUST cite file:line at the sha found from the live artifact or the deployment record, never a branch head or the latest tag. Behaviour comes from production data and dates from the deployment record. Code alone is a hypothesis; an absence claim needs data.

rules.title: Agent output is a lead
rules.statement: Output from an agent, a retrieval system or a review bot MUST be treated as a lead, never as evidence. Every cited line is re-read by the author before use; a quoted line is not verbatim until checked.

rules.title: Read sources in full
rules.statement: A summary, digest or excerpt MUST NOT stand in for its source. The source is read in full, and the deliverable says which sources were read in full and which were not.

rules.title: Compute a headline number twice
rules.statement: A number that leads a deliverable MUST be computed a second, different way before it is reported. Counts from two systems with different identity models are never divided without the join. A number that moves between identical runs is a harness artefact, not a result.

rules.title: Sweep after one defect
rules.statement: When one defect is found, the pattern MUST be named and every surface it could affect swept, each reported as confirmed, not affected, or not checked.

rules.title: Refute before filing
rules.statement: A finding against someone else's code MUST be verified twice before it is filed, the second pass trying to refute it.

rules.title: Re-read before asserting
rules.statement: A file's current state MUST be re-read before it is asserted or edited, in particular after a checkout, stash or rebase. A change request's current state is re-read before it is updated.

rules.title: Survey before building
rules.statement: Before custom code is written, established tools MUST be surveyed (tool, data source, maintenance, fit), the survey recorded and the pick named; custom code covers only the gap. When a partner's or vendor's documents define a mechanism, that definition is followed rather than a new mode invented.

rules.title: Record what a source taught
rules.statement: Research MUST produce a dated document in the topic's folder: the question, the sources read (full or partial), the method, the findings with evidence, the open questions and the exact commands, so it is never redone. An earlier document is never overwritten.

rules.title: Open points stay open
rules.statement: A point a reviewer raised, or one the decider has not settled, MUST be presented as open: the options, who decides, by when. Before a repository document or plan is pushed, every normative sentence that settles a question is listed for the decider.

rules.title: Misses are reported as misses
rules.statement: A missed target, a skipped step or a scope cut MUST be stated in the headline, in plain words, without apology language and without hedging.

rules.title: Shared deliverables are technical only
rules.statement: A shared deliverable MUST name no individual, assign no blame or credit, read no one's motives, and use no "ours" and "yours"; it names the system and who picks it up.

rules.title: Verbatim words
rules.statement: When the decider gives words, they MUST be used verbatim. When the decider accepts a draft, polishing stops.

rules.title: A draft promises nothing its signer did not say
rules.statement: A draft in someone's name MUST promise nothing they did not say: it gives the findings, a suggested order and what good looks like, and the owner named in the plan carries the work.

rules.title: Findings on the introducing change, at the head sha
rules.statement: A review finding MUST be posted only on the change that introduced the code, verified at that change's head sha, and limited to what is essential.

rules.title: One finding per thread, in Conventional Comments
rules.statement: Each inline thread MUST carry one finding with a Conventional Comments label, the defect, file:line, the consequence, the rule broken, the required behaviour, and at most one suggestion. No hedges.

rules.title: The summary carries the decision
rules.statement: The review summary MUST be two to four lines and end with the decision: approve, request changes, or needs a decider.

rules.title: Mutate before trusting a test
rules.statement: A test MUST be judged against the code it exercises, never from its body or name. One condition the change adds is inverted and the suite run; a mutant the suite does not catch is a finding that names the missing case; a mutant that changed nothing proves nothing. The count of mutants and catches is reported.
rules.notes: The probe (invert one condition, run the suite, restore) is rewritten from code-review-and-quality (addyosmani/agent-skills); the count and the dead-mutant reading are the author's.

rules.title: Review rounds fix only real defects
rules.statement: A review round MUST fix real defects only. A cosmetic bot suggestion gets a one-line verdict and no push. On the author's own change every bot thread is answered (fixed, or refuted with evidence) and resolved; on another author's change the reply is left and the author resolves.

rules.title: Confirm the diff is absent before merging
rules.statement: Before a change is reported on, merged or closed, its diff MUST be confirmed absent from the target. A stacked change is checked against its parent's tip, and a conflict resolution is re-diffed against the target's current file.

rules.title: Adversarial self-review before showing
rules.statement: Every plan, finding, draft and change MUST be reviewed adversarially before it is shown: which claim rests on a source not opened in this session, which number was recalled rather than computed, which action does damage if the premise is wrong. Before any push, merge or live change, what the review finds is fixed first.

rules.title: Sort proposals by what ships
rules.statement: A speed, cost or infrastructure proposal MUST be sorted into internals-only or changes the released artifact (versioning, signing, distribution). The second kind needs a strong reason, stated.

rules.title: One dependency per change
rules.statement: A dependency upgrade MUST be reviewed against its changelog, isolated per package, verified by the test suite before and after, with the lockfile diff reviewed and the lockfile never edited by hand.

rules.title: Test and infrastructure work leaves shipped code alone
rules.statement: Test or infrastructure work MUST NOT change shipped code without an explicit ask. A negative-test probe runs in a worktree or a temporary repository, never on a checkout with uncommitted work.

rules.title: One plan file, dated steps with done-when
rules.statement: A plan MUST be one file per project or topic, with dated steps of at most three days, each with one owner, a date the owner named, and a "done when" someone else can check. Each step is reversible or says how it is undone.

rules.title: Assumptions tied to tests
rules.statement: Every assumption MUST be numbered and tied to the test, query or vendor answer that proves it, or marked open. The first step attacks the riskiest assumption, in vertical slices that work end to end.

rules.title: Cut order and never-cut list
rules.statement: A plan MUST carry the order in which work is cut if time runs short and the list that is never cut. A slip is reported before its date, a scope cut goes in the headline, and a baseline is never moved silently.

rules.title: Behaviour change stated up front
rules.statement: A design or plan MUST say whether it breaks existing behaviour, the exact behaviour change and what was parked, and carry a failure-mode table (failure, allowed impact, mechanism, test) and a per-client compatibility table. New pieces degrade alone; one bug never stops the business.

rules.title: Gates carry escalation ladders
rules.statement: Any queue, gate or rule a plan proposes MUST carry its escalation ladder: self-service, a named decider role, the lanes that pass without the decider, a ceiling, each with a response time.

rules.title: No resourcing, trivia or blocker words
rules.statement: A plan MUST NOT contain headcount or resourcing, operational trivia, alarm phrases (blocker, urgent, critical) in a repository document, or a follow-up-ticket line in place of a decision.

rules.title: Decisions in the decider's words
rules.statement: A plan MUST lay out options; the decision MUST be recorded in the decider's own words with who decides and by when. The decider approves; each delivery step names a team or role as its owner.

rules.title: Newest production version
rules.statement: A design MUST use the newest version the platform runs in production, after checking availability. It is never designed on a beta and never chooses an older version to stay compatible with something not in production.

rules.title: Platform changes prove out on staging
rules.statement: A platform or CI change MUST prove out on staging and be validated there before production.

rules.title: Rounds over the frontier
rules.statement: A grilling MUST ask the whole frontier in one round: every question whose prerequisites are settled, numbered, each with a recommended answer worded so that "yes" accepts it. A question that depends on another still open belongs to a later round.

rules.title: Facts are the agent's job
rules.statement: A fact available from the environment MUST be looked up, never asked. Only decisions go to the decider.

rules.title: The session ends when the frontier is empty
rules.statement: An agent MUST NOT act on a plan until the decider confirms a shared understanding. Every settled decision MUST be recorded in the plan's Decisions table or as a decision record.

rules.title: A record for a hard-to-reverse, surprising trade-off
rules.statement: An architecture decision record MUST be written only when all three hold: the decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and the result of a real trade-off. One paragraph is enough.

rules.title: Glossary terms are opinionated and implementation-free
rules.statement: GLOSSARY.md MUST pick one term per concept, list the words to avoid, define what the thing is in one or two sentences, and carry no implementation detail.

rules.title: Knowledge in tables with calibration
rules.statement: Shared knowledge MUST go where the second reader can reach it, in the repository, as tables with fixed columns and calibration labelled honestly ("unverified", never blank) for glossaries, research documents and plan tables; the decision record is the prose exception, one paragraph.

rules.title: Records carry no names
rules.statement: A decision record, glossary or research document MUST name systems and roles, never individuals.

rules.title: One file per topic, never another's file
rules.statement: A plan, record or research document MUST be one file per topic. Before a write, the path is checked; a file not created in this session is not overwritten.

rules.title: Conflicts with a record are surfaced
rules.statement: Output that contradicts an existing decision record MUST say so and why it is worth reopening, never override it silently.
rules.notes: Rewritten from the domain conventions of setup-matt-pocock-skills (mattpocock/skills).

rules.title: One ticket per real work item
rules.statement: Tickets MUST be one per real work item, never one per checklist step. Each is a vertical slice, demoable or verifiable on its own and sized to one working session.

rules.title: Acceptance and blockers
rules.statement: Every ticket MUST carry what to build from the user's perspective, acceptance criteria someone else can check, and the tickets that block it, as native dependency links where the tracker has them.

rules.title: No identifiers, secrets or names
rules.statement: A ticket or change description MUST NOT carry infrastructure identifiers, secret paths, partner URLs or colleagues' names. It describes the step and points to the internal runbook.

rules.title: Full links
rules.statement: Every reference to another change or ticket MUST be a full link, never a bare number.

rules.title: Approval before publishing
rules.statement: The breakdown MUST be shown and approved in the conversation before anything is published. Publishing is a post and waits for its go-ahead (ASK-3). The parent item is never closed or edited by the breakdown.

rules.title: Wide refactors use expand and contract
rules.statement: A mechanical change whose blast radius spans the codebase MUST be sequenced as expand, migrate in batches, contract, each batch its own ticket, so every step keeps the checks passing.

rules.title: Seams agreed before tests
rules.statement: Tests MUST be written at seams agreed with the decider first, each proposed seam with a line on what it catches and what it misses.

rules.title: Red before green
rules.statement: The failing test MUST be written first and only enough code to pass it follows: one seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle. A refactor is its own slice after green (SLICE-3), not part of the loop.

rules.title: Expected values from an independent source
rules.statement: An expected value MUST come from a known-good literal, a worked example or the specification, with the derivation in the test, never recomputed the way the code computes it. A test that asserts only a range or a sign does not count.

rules.title: Mock only at system boundaries
rules.statement: Mocks MUST sit only at external services, time, randomness and the file system, never at the code under test, pure functions, value objects or internal collaborators.

rules.title: Gate on exit codes
rules.statement: A commit MUST be gated on the checks' exit codes (check && test && git commit), never on output that is printed and ignored. A check that passed on unchanged code is not re-run for reassurance.

rules.title: Suites one at a time against shared state
rules.statement: Test suites that share a database or external state MUST run one at a time, and results are compared by named failures, not counts.

rules.title: Enumerate branches before repairing
rules.statement: Before a failing test is repaired, the branches the code takes MUST be enumerated. A better-shaped test replaces a patched one, and the mutation check (REVIEW-4) confirms it.

rules.title: One change per step, reviewable in one sitting
rules.statement: Work MUST land as small, independently reviewable pieces with clear acceptance, one pull request per plan step, so the review load stays low.

rules.title: Nothing half-done reaches the shared branch
rules.statement: A step MUST be merged complete, with its tests, documentation and, where the repository keeps one, its changelog entry, or not at all. Incomplete work stays behind a flag or on its branch.

rules.title: Scope discipline
rules.statement: A change MUST touch only what the step requires. Adjacent cleanups, modernised syntax and unrelated refactors are noted and left for their own step.

rules.title: Verify once per change
rules.statement: Each verification command MUST run after a change that could affect it, and is not repeated on unchanged code.

rules.title: Stage by path and read the index
rules.statement: Changes MUST be staged by path, as whole files by path or as hunks through git apply --cached when another session may have edited the file, and git diff --cached --stat is read before the commit (STAGE-1).

rules.title: A go-ahead per commit, per push, per post
rules.statement: Every commit, push and post MUST wait for its own go-ahead. Approval in one context does not extend to the next (ASK-1, ASK-2, ASK-3).

rules.title: Auto-merge only where allowed
rules.statement: Auto-merge MUST be armed only where the decider allowed it for that repository and branch. A merge to a release branch is a deliberate human act.

rules.title: Fresh new files, confirmed deletions
rules.statement: Before a new file is written its path MUST be confirmed absent; before a deletion the file is confirmed untracked, or its removal is confirmed by the decider.

rules.title: Never print a secret
rules.statement: A secret MUST never be printed. Give the variable name, file:line, length or hash. Token-bearing lines are excluded before a log is summarised, and a masking regex is never trusted.

rules.title: Production is read-only
rules.statement: Production systems and data MUST be treated as read-only unless the decider says otherwise for that specific action.

rules.title: Deep modules
rules.statement: A module MUST hide a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam and testable through that interface. Depth is payback for callers and locality for maintainers.

rules.title: The interface is the test surface
rules.statement: Tests MUST cross the same seam callers do. A test that has to reach past the interface shows the module is the wrong shape.

rules.title: Two adapters make a seam
rules.statement: A seam MUST NOT be introduced until something varies across it. One adapter is a hypothetical seam and plain indirection.

rules.title: Replace tests after deepening
rules.statement: After a cluster of shallow modules is deepened, the tests at the old modules MUST be deleted and replaced by tests at the new interface.

rules.title: Design it twice, with consent
rules.statement: Alternative interfaces MUST be explored with parallel agents only after the decider agreed to the fan-out. Otherwise one design is explored at a time.
rules.notes: Rewritten from codebase-design (mattpocock/skills), after Ousterhout's design it twice.

rules.title: One block in the repository's agent file
rules.statement: The repository's AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md MUST carry one "Rules that bind" block that points at docs/agents/ and .agentic-sdlc.json. The file that exists is edited; a second one is never created beside it. When neither file exists, the decider is asked which one to create; the skill never picks.

rules.title: Tracker and labels recorded first
rules.statement: Where tickets live and which labels are used MUST be recorded in docs/agents/tracker.md before any skill publishes a ticket.

rules.title: Mechanisms arrive as a reviewed change
rules.statement: The repository configuration, the reusable workflow and the ruleset import MUST land as a reviewed pull request, never silently.

rules.title: An untraceable gated command is confirmed
rules.statement: When a command mentions a commit, a push, a bulk add or a forge write but the parser cannot trace it to a git, gh or glab invocation (a variable, an interpreter, an unusual wrapper), the command MUST be confirmed by the user before it runs.
rules.fix: Run the git, gh or glab command directly so the hook can read it, or confirm this one yourself.

rules.title: An untraced command is suspicious when configured
rules.statement: When the parser cannot trace a command to a git, gh or glab invocation and trace.untracked is ask or deny, the hook MUST answer with that decision, unless every simple command in it is a read-only program.
rules.fix: Run the git, gh or glab command directly so the hook can trace it, or set trace.untracked to allow.

rules.title: Hook bypass flags are refused
rules.statement: An agent MUST NOT skip the repository's hooks: git commit or git push with --no-verify (or commit -n), git -c core.hooksPath=…, include.path=… or an alias override on the command line, and git config setting core.hooksPath or include.path are refused.
rules.fix: Run the command without the flag and let the hooks run; if a hook is wrong, fix the hook.

rules.title: The guard's own configuration is changed knowingly
rules.statement: An agent's edit to .agentic-sdlc.json, a git hook, .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json or .pre-commit-config.yaml MUST be confirmed by the user before it is written.
rules.fix: Say what the edit changes in the guard and why; write it when the user says yes.

rules.title: Reading a secret file asks
rules.statement: Reading, grepping, copying or sending a file that by name holds credentials (.env files, private keys, .netrc, .npmrc, .pypirc, credentials.json, PEM and keystore files) MUST be confirmed by the user before it happens.
rules.fix: Name the variable or the file and its length or hash instead; read the file only when the user says yes.

conformance: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT and MAY in the statements are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 (RFC 2119, RFC 8174) when, and only when, they appear in all capitals. A rule whose mechanism lists hook can be switched off for a repository through .agentic-sdlc.json; the statement names the key.
